messages.subject: Bernoulli family for presence/absence data
parts:
I would like to run a bayesian Bernoulli regression model using R-INLA. I have presence-absence data (1's and 0's) for every 100mX100m pixel within the study space (grid data), as well as several covariates (unique data points for each presence/absence pixel). Looking through this help forum, it looks like most people looking at Bernoulli likelihoods are using family=binomial in R-INLA. But how could Bernoulli and Binomial be interchangeable, given that Binomial involves adding up all the 1's and 0's? I don't want to add them up; rather, I would like to proceed with unique presence/absence values and covariate values for each pixel. Does anyone have any suggestions?

Here is my mesh:


Here is the mesh with data points added (in red). There are so many points that it just looks like the mesh is completely filled in.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Bernoulli family for presence/absence data
parts:
Hi

bernoulli is just a synomym for binomial with 1 trial and only
family="binomial",Ntrials=n,
is implemented, just set n=rep(1, number.of.data)

H
